content_units: A Friendly Reply You Can Send

Animation definitely isn’t just for kids — it’s a medium, not a genre. It can do crime, romance, war, philosophy, sci-fi, memoir, and surreal drama just as well as live action, sometimes even better because it isn’t limited by physical reality.
Option 1:   Perfect Blue   (Japan)   A psychological thriller about fame, identity, and paranoia that feels as intense as any live-action suspense film.     Style:   dark anime / mind-bending drama
Option 2:   Persepolis   (France/Iran)   A sharp, funny, and deeply human autobiographical story about growing up during political upheaval.     Style:   graphic black-and-white memoir
Option 3:   Waltz with Bashir   (Israel)   A haunting animated documentary that uses memory and surreal imagery to explore war and trauma.     Style:   documentary / reflective war drama

Option 4:   BoJack Horseman   (United States)   Starts like a comedy about a washed-up sitcom star and turns into one of the smartest shows about depression, ego, and self-sabotage.     Style:   satirical series / emotional character study

Option 5:   The Triplets of Belleville   (France)   Almost wordless, visually eccentric, and wildly charming — proof that animation can be sophisticated, strange, and unmistakably auteur-driven.     Style:   stylized international art-comedy

Option 6:   Love, Death & Robots   (International/US)   An anthology of short animated stories ranging from brutal sci-fi to dark comedy, with each episode using a different visual approach.     Style:   anthology / experimental adult sci-fi
A Good Way to Frame It

If someone says animation is only for kids, I’d say: “Some animation is made for children, sure — just like some live-action movies are. But animation itself is simply a way of telling stories. It can be funny, disturbing, political, intimate, or experimental. The range goes from memoirs and documentaries to psychological thrillers and adult comedies, so writing it off is kind of like saying all novels are for children because picture books exist.”
